# <img src="../Hexagon_MetaProViz.png" align="right" width="200" />

This vignette demonstrates the `id_processing()` workflow for feature metadata in **MetaProViz**. The function is designed to orchestrate ID-space exploration and optional downstream processing in a transparent way rather than hide the individual helper functions. The workflow can quantify the current ID space, optionally run automatic seed-ID compatibility handling, and then optionally continue with either ID translation or ID traversal.

The vignette uses the packaged `tissue_meta` example. This dataset is the package-safe equivalent of the older Revision-branch feature-metadata workflow, but the workflow shown here intentionally replaces the previously manual ID handling with the automatic compatibility handling now available through `seed_id_compatibility_check()`.

```{r load-packages, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(MetaProViz)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)

data(tissue_meta)

Tissue_MetaData <- tissue_meta %>%
    filter(!grepl("^X\\s*-\\s*\\d+$", Metabolite))
```

The workflow-managed identifier namespaces are currently `HMDB`, `KEGG`, `CHEBI`, and `PUBCHEM`. These columns are treated as the canonical ID-space columns, while other metadata columns such as names, pathway classes, or platform information are preserved across all workflow stages.

## Default workflow: exploration only

The current default behavior is intentionally conservative. By default, `id_processing()` performs the initial ID-space quantification and then stops. In particular, `run_compatibility_check = FALSE`, `run_translation = FALSE`, `run_traversal = FALSE`, and `verbose = FALSE` by default. This means that users explicitly opt into the more opinionated or more computationally involved processing steps.

`verbose` controls detailed logging from the delegated compatibility and traversal helpers. The `id_processing()` workflow itself always prints its stage progress and result overview.

The explicit default call is shown below with every parameter written out:

```{r id-processing-default, eval=TRUE}
id_default <- id_processing(
    data = Tissue_MetaData,
    id_types = c("HMDB", "KEGG", "CHEBI", "PUBCHEM"),
    delimiter = c(";", ","),
    run_compatibility_check = FALSE,
    handle_partially_compatible = TRUE,
    handle_completely_incompatible = TRUE,
    completely_incompatible_priority = c("HMDB", "CHEBI", "PUBCHEM", "KEGG"),
    run_translation = FALSE,
    translation_from = NULL,
    translation_to = NULL,
    translation_summary = FALSE,
    run_traversal = FALSE,
    edge_table = NULL,
    compare_name_col = "Metabolite",
    save_plot = NULL,
    save_table = NULL,
    print_plot = FALSE,
    verbose = FALSE,
    path = NULL
)
```

This default run is useful when the first goal is simply to understand the current identifier coverage and overlap structure before deciding whether compatibility handling, translation, or traversal should be applied.

```{r id-processing-default-out, eval=TRUE}
names(id_default)
names(id_default$Data)
names(id_default$Plot)
names(id_default$Workflow)
head(id_default$Data$id_count_summary)
head(id_default$Data$compare_pk_summary_by_stage$input)
head(id_default$Data$count_id_tables_by_stage$input$HMDB)
```

## Compatibility-check workflow

If you want the function to assess whether multiple IDs assigned to the same feature row are mutually compatible, enable the compatibility step explicitly. With the current defaults for the handling parameters, partially compatible and completely incompatible rows will be handled automatically once the compatibility step is enabled.

```{r id-processing-qc, eval=TRUE}
id_qc <- id_processing(
    data = Tissue_MetaData,
    id_types = c("HMDB", "KEGG", "CHEBI", "PUBCHEM"),
    delimiter = c(";", ","),
    run_compatibility_check = TRUE,
    handle_partially_compatible = TRUE,
    handle_completely_incompatible = TRUE,
    completely_incompatible_priority = c("HMDB", "CHEBI", "PUBCHEM", "KEGG"),
    run_translation = FALSE,
    translation_from = NULL,
    translation_to = NULL,
    translation_summary = FALSE,
    run_traversal = FALSE,
    edge_table = NULL,
    compare_name_col = "Metabolite",
    save_plot = NULL,
    save_table = NULL,
    print_plot = FALSE,
    verbose = FALSE,
    path = NULL
)
```

```{r id-processing-qc-out, eval=TRUE}
head(id_qc$Data$input[, c("Metabolite", "HMDB", "KEGG", "CHEBI", "PUBCHEM")])
head(id_qc$Data$after_compatibility[, c("Metabolite", "HMDB", "KEGG", "CHEBI", "PUBCHEM")])
head(id_qc$Data$id_count_summary)
id_qc$Workflow$steps_run
names(id_qc$Data$compatibility)
id_qc$Workflow$result_overview_text
```

## Translation workflow

If you want to translate one namespace into one or more others, enable the translation step explicitly. Translation and traversal are intentionally mutually exclusive within a single run so that each run remains straightforward to interpret.

```{r id-processing-translation, eval=TRUE}
id_translation <- id_processing(
    data = Tissue_MetaData,
    id_types = c("HMDB", "KEGG", "CHEBI", "PUBCHEM"),
    delimiter = c(";", ","),
    run_compatibility_check = TRUE,
    handle_partially_compatible = TRUE,
    handle_completely_incompatible = TRUE,
    completely_incompatible_priority = c("HMDB", "CHEBI", "PUBCHEM", "KEGG"),
    run_translation = TRUE,
    translation_from = "PUBCHEM",
    translation_to = c("HMDB", "KEGG"),
    translation_summary = FALSE,
    run_traversal = FALSE,
    edge_table = NULL,
    compare_name_col = "Metabolite",
    save_plot = NULL,
    save_table = NULL,
    print_plot = FALSE,
    verbose = FALSE,
    path = NULL
)
```

```{r id-processing-translation-out, eval=TRUE}
head(id_translation$Data$after_translation[, c("Metabolite", "PUBCHEM", "HMDB", "KEGG")])
id_translation$Data$id_count_summary
names(id_translation$Data$translation)
head(id_translation$Data$translation$input)
head(id_translation$Data$translation$translated_ids)
```

## Traversal workflow

If you want to expand the seed ID space through the RaMP mapping graph, enable traversal explicitly. This is not part of the default behavior.

```{r id-processing-traversal, eval=TRUE}
id_traversal <- id_processing(
    data = Tissue_MetaData,
    id_types = c("HMDB", "KEGG", "CHEBI", "PUBCHEM"),
    delimiter = c(";", ","),
    run_compatibility_check = TRUE,
    handle_partially_compatible = TRUE,
    handle_completely_incompatible = TRUE,
    completely_incompatible_priority = c("HMDB", "CHEBI", "PUBCHEM", "KEGG"),
    run_translation = FALSE,
    translation_from = NULL,
    translation_to = NULL,
    translation_summary = FALSE,
    run_traversal = TRUE,
    edge_table = NULL,
    compare_name_col = "Metabolite",
    save_plot = NULL,
    save_table = NULL,
    print_plot = FALSE,
    verbose = FALSE,
    path = NULL
)
```

### Inspecting the traversal return object

The traversal workflow returns stage metadata, QC results, and traversal artifacts in their respective `Data` and `Plot` sections. `Workflow` records only the configuration and execution summary.

```{r id-processing-traversal-structure, eval=TRUE}
names(id_traversal)
names(id_traversal$Data)
names(id_traversal$Plot)
names(id_traversal$Workflow)
names(id_traversal$Data$traversal)
```

The `Data` section contains the input metadata and the metadata produced by each enabled stage:

```{r id-processing-traversal-data-1, eval=TRUE}
head(id_traversal$Data$input[, c("Metabolite", "HMDB", "KEGG", "CHEBI", "PUBCHEM")])
head(id_traversal$Data$after_compatibility[, c("Metabolite", "HMDB", "KEGG", "CHEBI", "PUBCHEM")])
head(id_traversal$Data$after_traversal[, c("Metabolite", "HMDB", "KEGG", "CHEBI", "PUBCHEM")])
```

The stage-wise ID-count summary shows whether traversal increased the represented ID space overall and in which namespaces those gains occurred:

```{r id-processing-traversal-data-2, eval=FALSE}
id_traversal$Data$id_count_summary
subset(id_traversal$Data$id_count_summary, namespace == "HMDB")
subset(id_traversal$Data$id_count_summary, namespace == "KEGG")
subset(id_traversal$Data$id_count_summary, namespace == "CHEBI")
subset(id_traversal$Data$id_count_summary, namespace == "PUBCHEM")
```

The stage-wise `compare_pk()` summary tables can be compared directly across stages:

```{r id-processing-traversal-data-3, eval=TRUE}
names(id_traversal$Data$compare_pk_summary_by_stage)
head(id_traversal$Data$compare_pk_summary_by_stage$input)
head(id_traversal$Data$compare_pk_summary_by_stage$after_compatibility)
head(id_traversal$Data$compare_pk_summary_by_stage$after_traversal)
```

The underlying `count_id()` tables are also retained for each stage and namespace:

```{r id-processing-traversal-data-4, eval=TRUE}
names(id_traversal$Data$count_id_tables_by_stage)
names(id_traversal$Data$count_id_tables_by_stage$input)
head(id_traversal$Data$count_id_tables_by_stage$input$HMDB)
head(id_traversal$Data$count_id_tables_by_stage$after_traversal$HMDB)
head(id_traversal$Data$count_id_tables_by_stage$after_traversal$KEGG)
```

### Inspecting the raw traversal artifacts

The traversal-specific tables are stored once in `id_traversal$Data$traversal`; the expanded feature metadata is the `after_traversal` stage above.

```{r id-processing-traversal-raw-1, eval=TRUE}
head(id_traversal$Data$traversal$pair_compatibility)
head(id_traversal$Data$traversal$prior_knowledge_edges)
```

The pair-level compatibility table helps explain which seed-ID pairs were coherent before expansion:

```{r id-processing-traversal-raw-2, eval=TRUE}
colnames(id_traversal$Data$traversal$pair_compatibility)
unique(id_traversal$Data$traversal$pair_compatibility$compatibility_path)
table(id_traversal$Data$traversal$pair_compatibility$all_seed_ids_compatible, useNA = "ifany")
```

The edge table helps interpret the mechanistic basis of the traversal itself:

```{r id-processing-traversal-raw-3, eval=TRUE}
colnames(id_traversal$Data$traversal$prior_knowledge_edges)
head(id_traversal$Data$traversal$prior_knowledge_edges[, c("id1", "type1", "id2", "type2")])
```

### Inspecting workflow metadata and plots

```{r id-processing-traversal-workflow, eval=TRUE}
id_traversal$Workflow$settings
id_traversal$Workflow$steps_run
id_traversal$Workflow$stage_messages
id_traversal$Workflow$result_overview_text
```

```{r id-processing-traversal-plots, eval=TRUE}
names(id_traversal$Plot$compare_pk_by_stage)
names(id_traversal$Plot$count_id_by_stage)
id_traversal$Plot$compare_pk_by_stage$input
id_traversal$Plot$compare_pk_by_stage$after_traversal
id_traversal$Plot$count_id_by_stage$after_traversal$HMDB
id_traversal$Plot$count_id_by_stage$after_traversal$KEGG
```

Taken together, these checks provide a detailed audit trail for a traversal run: the feature metadata before and after each stage, the change in the quantifiable ID space, the raw compatibility information, the raw graph edges used for traversal, and the plots and textual summaries that explain what happened.

## Notes

`equivalent_id()` is intentionally not part of `id_processing()` yet. If you want additional ambiguity-aware within-namespace expansion after this workflow, run `equivalent_id()` afterwards on the final feature metadata.
